# Twitch (4 endpoints)

## Endpoints

| Resource | Params | Credits | Description |
|----------|--------|---------|-------------|
| /profile | `handle` | 1 | Get Twitch streamer profile |
| /clip | `url` | 1 | Get Twitch clip details |
| /user/videos | `handle` | 1 | List a Twitch user's videos |
| /user/schedule | `handle` | 1 | Get a Twitch user's stream schedule |

### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- *(none)* — no required parameters.

## Parameter Details

- `handle`: Twitch username
- `url`: Full URL of the Twitch clip
- `handle (/user/videos)`: Twitch username.
- `filter_by` *(optional, enum: HIGHLIGHT | ARCHIVE | UPLOAD)*: Filter the returned videos by type — `HIGHLIGHT`, `ARCHIVE`, or `UPLOAD`.
- `sort_by` *(optional, enum: TIME | VIEWS)*: Sort order — `TIME` (newest first) or `VIEWS`.
- `handle (/user/schedule)`: Twitch username.

## Field Maps


The `profile` endpoint returns an `Author` response normalized by the `twitch-author` field map, and `clip` returns a `Post` normalized by `twitch-post`. Twitch clip responses are nested under `clip.*` upstream; the field map flattens them. Both include computed fields under `data.computed`.

## Example

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/twitch/profile?handle=ninja" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```
